picks.excerpt: An exclusive look inside Google's plan for the AI glasses it and Samsung will ship this fall - the designs, the privacy backlash it wants to avoid, and how it intends to fight Meta and Apple for a place on your face.
picks.rationale: Exclusive, same-day look inside the fall Google/Samsung AI glasses: it frames the privacy design problem rather than reporting a spec, which is the decision designers actually face.

picks.excerpt: 1X's Neo Beta home robot shows off new hands that can assemble LEGO, unzip a jacket and open a snack bag - the most human-like manipulation yet from a consumer humanoid.
picks.rationale: A concrete, demonstrable manipulation leap on a consumer humanoid - fresh, and a different device class from the glasses/phone bulk of the pool.

picks.excerpt: The Signal Ring, from an ex-Google health lead, drops sleep scores and step counts entirely to chase one thing: cuffless, calibration-free blood pressure sensing that Apple and Samsung haven't cracked.
picks.rationale: A wearable that subtracts features to solve one hard sensing problem - a sharp product-scoping lesson, and more novel than the Oura Ring 5 iteration review in the same pool.

picks.excerpt: nubia unveils the NaviX Ultra, its take on the 'AI agentic phone' - the concept Chinese phone makers are racing to define, with an on-device agent driving the whole UI.
picks.rationale: An agent-driven phone UI shipping as a real product - the clearest look yet at what the 'agentic phone' interface actually becomes once it leaves the concept deck.

picks.excerpt: PrismML released Bonsai 27B, claiming it's the first model of that size that actually runs on an iPhone - a push to move frontier-class on-device AI onto phone silicon.
picks.rationale: A 27B model claimed to run on an iPhone redraws the ceiling for on-device AI - the constraint that decides which features can stay local and private.
